definitions.explanation: A burial site where the remains of the deceased are interred, typically a family grave with a stone marker located in temple grounds or a cemetery. Visiting and maintaining graves is an important Japanese cultural practice.

examples.japanese: お{墓|はか}に{花|はな}を{供|そな}えた。
examples.english: I placed flowers at the grave.

examples.japanese: お{盆|ぼん}にお{墓|はか}{参|まい}りに{行|い}く。
examples.english: I visit the grave during Obon.

examples.japanese: {祖父母|そふぼ}のお{墓|はか}は{田舎|いなか}の{寺|てら}の{境内|けいだい}にあり、{毎年|まいとし}{家族|かぞく}で{掃除|そうじ}に{行|い}っている。
examples.english: My grandparents' grave is in the grounds of a temple in the countryside, and every year our family goes to clean it.

notes:
The polite form of {墓|はか} (grave), with the honorific prefix お. In everyday speech, お{墓|はか} is the standard form — using {墓|はか} without お can sound blunt or overly direct.

USAGE:
- Japanese graves are typically family graves ({家族|かぞく}{墓|ぼ}) located in temple or cemetery grounds
- Visiting and maintaining the grave is an important cultural practice, especially during お{盆|ぼん} (mid-August) and お{彼岸|ひがん} (equinox periods)
- The act of visiting a grave is called お{墓|はか}{参|まい}り
- In modern Japan, discussions about graves also include alternative burial styles like {納骨堂|のうこつどう} (columbariums) and {樹木葬|じゅもくそう} (tree burial)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{墓|はか}{参|まい}り: visiting a grave
- お{墓|はか}を{建|た}てる: to build/erect a grave
- お{墓|はか}を{掃除|そうじ}する: to clean a grave
- お{墓|はか}に{入|はい}る: to be buried (lit. to enter the grave)
- お{墓|はか}の{前|まえ}で{手|て}を{合|あ}わせる: to put one's hands together in prayer before the grave

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {墓地|ぼち}: cemetery, graveyard — the area where graves are located
- {墓石|ぼせき}: gravestone, tombstone — the stone marker itself
- {霊園|れいえん}: memorial park, cemetery — a more modern, park-like cemetery
